lyrics:
[Intro: crying steel guitar, two-step shuffle]

[Verse 1: female alto, conversational drawl]
She came home from a ski trip with a look I'd seen before
On my own face in a mirror, nineteen eighty-four
Kept saying "the air out there," kept saying "you should see"
I knew right then that I'd been beat by geography

[Chorus: full band, steel and fiddle, harmony]
Colorado got my girl
Got her boots, got her dog, got her whole wide world
I raised her on red dirt and sweet iced tea
But the Rockies sang a little louder than me
I ain't mad, I'm just short one pearl
Colorado got my girl

[Verse 2: alto, band easy behind her]
We loaded up the trailer in a pouring rain
Her daddy checked the tires three times, then checked again
She hugged me in the driveway, said, "Mama, please don't cry"
I said, "Baby, this is allergies," and looked up at the sky

[Chorus: full band, steel and fiddle, harmony]
Colorado got my girl
Got her boots, got her dog, got her whole wide world
I raised her on red dirt and sweet iced tea
But the Rockies sang a little louder than me
I ain't mad, I'm just short one pearl
Colorado got my girl

[Bridge: steel guitar and voice, slower]
My mama stood right here when I left for Tennessee
I didn't understand that look
Till it was on me

[Final Chorus: full band, a second harmony joins]
Colorado got my girl
Got her boots, got her dog, got her whole wide world
I raised her on red dirt and sweet iced tea
But the Rockies sang a little louder than me
She sounds so happy on the phone it hurts
Colorado, be good to my girl

[Outro: steel guitar, a phone buzz, spoken]
"Made it. It snowed. I love it."
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 120 BPM two-step shuffle, 4/4, E major. A dance-hall sway that keeps moving while the words ache.

VOICE: Female alto, plain, warm and dry-humoured, with a Southern drawl. She sings like she is talking over a kitchen counter. A close harmony joins in the choruses. She reads a text message aloud at the end.

INSTRUMENTS: Pedal steel guitar leading, fiddle, a twangy electric guitar, acoustic rhythm guitar, a walking bass, shuffle drums with brushes on the snare, honky-tonk piano.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, steel guitar. 0:10 Verse 1. 0:40 Chorus 1. 1:08 Verse 2. 1:38 Chorus 2. 2:06 Bridge, steel and voice. 2:26 Final chorus. 2:56 Outro, a phone buzz and the read-out message at 3:06.

PRODUCTION & MIX: A 1990s-style country band recorded with present-day clarity: steel and fiddle up front, drums soft, voice natural.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: 'Baby, this is allergies' at 1:32.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original loses a man to a place. This one loses a daughter to one, and the singer is old enough to remember doing the same thing to her own mother.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Recognition, brave face, understanding, blessing.
